items.q2: کیا آپ جان داروں کی کچھ مزید خصوصیات بتا سکتے ہیں؟

items.a: They get rid of wastes (excretion), they need water, they respond to their surroundings (e.g. plants grow towards light), and they have a fixed lifespan and die.

items.q: Tell few characteristics of a vehicle that are also found in living things.
items.q2: گاڑی کی چند ایسی خصوصیات بتائیں جو جان داروں میں بھی پائی جاتی ہیں۔

items.a: A vehicle moves, it uses fuel (like food) for energy, it takes in air and gives out exhaust gases (like breathing). But it cannot grow, reproduce or sense on its own, so it is non-living.

items.q: Look at the pictures of a mango tree and a goat. Analyze the differences and similarities between the characteristics of these two living things.
items.q2: آم کے درخت اور بکری کی تصویریں دیکھیں۔ ان دونوں جان داروں کی خصوصیات میں فرق اور مماثلتوں کا تجزیہ کریں۔
items.q3: د ام د ونې او وزې انځورونو ته وګورئ. د دې دوو ژوندیو د ځانګړنو توپیرونه او ورته والی وڅېړئ.
items.a: Similarities: both grow, respire and reproduce. Differences: the mango tree is green, makes its own food and cannot move from place to place; the goat is brown and white, depends on plants for food and can move about.
items.e: From the Venn diagram on this page.

items.a: Parts of a leaf: lamina (flat green blade), midrib (main central vein), veins (thin lines branching from the midrib) and petiole (the stalk joining the leaf to the stem). The leaf in the picture is oval with a pointed tip.

items.q: Did you ever think that what is the purpose of these colourful flowers?
items.q2: کیا آپ نے کبھی سوچا کہ ان رنگ برنگے پھولوں کا مقصد کیا ہے؟

items.a: Colourful flowers attract insects and birds, which carry pollen from flower to flower; this helps the flower to make fruits and seeds.

items.q: Have you ever thought that food is made by the leaves then how has the plant been formed by the seeds?
items.q2: کیا آپ نے کبھی سوچا کہ خوراک تو پتّے بناتے ہیں، پھر بیجوں سے پودا کیسے بن گیا؟

items.a: Only about 3% of Earth's water is fresh, and much of it is frozen in glaciers. Growing population, wastage and pollution of rivers and lakes leave less clean water, and rain does not fall evenly everywhere.

items.q: Is it possible that we have more resources than those of the past?

items.q: Why does climate change with distance from the equator?
items.q2: خطِ استوا سے فاصلے کے ساتھ آب و ہوا کیوں بدلتی ہے؟
items.q3: له استوا څخه د واټن سره اقلیم ولې بدلېږي؟
items.a: At the equator the Sun's rays fall vertically and are strong; farther away they fall more slanted and become weaker, so places get less heat and the climate becomes cooler towards the poles.

items.q: Why is the climate of Polar Zone very cold?
items.q2: منطقۂ قطبی کی آب و ہوا بہت ٹھنڈی کیوں ہے؟
items.q3: د قطبي سیمې اقلیم ولې ډېر سوړ دی؟
items.a: Because the Sun's rays fall there most slantingly and are very weak, so these areas receive the least heat.

items.q: In which zone, our country is located on the basis of climate? Explain.
items.q2: آب و ہوا کی بنیاد پر ہمارا ملک کس خطے میں واقع ہے؟ وضاحت کریں۔

items.a: Pakistan lies mainly in the Temperate Zone, north of the Tropic of Cancer and close to the Tropical Zone. So the south is hot (Sindh, Balochistan plains), while the high northern mountains are cold with snow in winter; most of the country has hot summers and cool winters.

items.q: What is the climate of these zones? Describe the reasons.

items.a: Tropical Zone — hot, because the Sun's rays fall vertically. Temperate Zone — mild, because the rays fall slantingly and are weaker. Polar Zone — coldest, because the rays are most slanted and weakest.

items.a: Yes, Mercury and Venus, whose orbits are closer to the Sun than the Earth's, sometimes pass between the Sun and the Earth. They look like tiny black dots crossing the Sun (called a transit), because they are very small and far away.

items.a: Religion — Mesopotamia: idol worship (each city had its own god); Egypt: many gods, Pharaohs hoped to become gods, belief in life after death; Indus Valley: worship of animals, trees and statues. Professions — Mesopotamia: farming, livestock breeding, fishing, trade; Egypt: farmer (wheat and barley), trade along the Nile; Indus Valley: farmers, traders and skilled workers. Buildings — Mesopotamia: Haikal towers about 150 feet high, large cities; Egypt: pyramids and large graveyards; Indus Valley: planned cities with good roads, drainage, large buildings, government offices and bathhouses. Art and Handicrafts — Mesopotamia: cuneiform writing on clay tablets, wheel, maps; Egypt: pictures of Pharaohs and sculptures of gods, mummies; Indus Valley: clay pots, carved seals, jewellery and tools.

items.q: What is meant by globe and map? Explain the difference.
items.q2: گلوب اور نقشے سے کیا مراد ہے؟ فرق واضح کریں۔
items.q3: له ګلوب او نقشې څه مراد دی؟ توپیر یې روښانه کړئ.
items.a: A globe is a round model of the earth like a ball; it shows the division of land and water, has a network of longitude and latitude lines, shows the complete world at a single look and rotates on its axis. A map shows the complete earth or any part of it (a locality, city, province or country) on paper or a plain surface and tells us where a place is situated. So a globe is round and shows the whole earth, while a map is flat and can show any part of it.

items.a: By using a scale — a fixed ratio between the actual distance on the ground and the distance on the map. For example, if 1 km = 1 cm, two places 6 km apart are shown 6 cm apart on the map.

items.a: Scale — shows the ratio between actual distance on the ground and distance on the map, so we can find real distances. Border — the four sides show where the map starts and ends. items.a: A plateau is land raised from its surroundings with steep sides and a plain centre. Pakistan has two plateaus. Potwar plateau: 350–375 m high, between the rivers Indus and Jhelum; it gets rain in winter and monsoon and much of it is cultivated; the Salt Range (with the Khewra salt mine) lies to its south; the rivers Sawan and Haro flow through it. Balochistan plateau: 600–1200 m high; its land is stony, dry and barren with little rain, so farming is possible only along rivers or with Karez irrigation; its important rivers are Zhob, Hangol, Hub, Dasht and Porali; people mostly do mining and grazing, and there are orchards in some areas.

items.a: Plains are almost flat land formed from the fertile soil brought by the Indus and its tributaries (Upper Indus Plain in Punjab, Lower Indus Plain in Sindh); with river water, fertile soil and suitable climate they are very good for agriculture, and most people there are farmers, traders or work in industry. Deserts get less than 10 inches (25 cm) of rain a year, have sand dunes and very few plants, are the hottest areas, and their land is barren; people keep livestock, use camels and lead nomadic lives. Pakistan's deserts are Thal (Punjab), Thar (Cholistan in Punjab, Nara in Sindh) and Kharan (Balochistan).

items.a: Height above sea level — the higher a place, the lower its temperature (mountains are cold, plains are hot). Distance from the sea — water heats and cools slowly, so coastal areas stay moderate, while places far from the sea are not moderated. Winds direction — winds blow from high to low pressure; winds from cold regions lower the temperature and winds from hot, dry regions raise it (Karachi stays moderate with sea winds, Lahore is hot in summer).

items.q: دی گئیں تصاویر کو دیکھ کر کہانی لکھیں۔ کہانی یوں بھی شروع ہو سکتی ہے: ”ایک دفعہ کا ذکر ہے کہ ایک لکڑ ہارا دریا کے کنارے لکڑیاں کاٹ رہا تھا ۔۔۔“

items.a: نمونہ — عنوان: ”دیانت داری کا انعام“ · ایک دفعہ کا ذکر ہے کہ ایک لکڑ ہارا دریا کے کنارے لکڑیاں کاٹ رہا تھا۔ اچانک اس کی کلہاڑی ہاتھ سے چھوٹ کر دریا میں جا گری۔ وہ بہت پریشان ہوا اور کنارے پر بیٹھ کر رونے لگا، کیوں کہ یہی کلہاڑی اس کی روزی کا ذریعہ تھی۔ اتنے میں دریا میں سے ایک نورانی بزرگ نمودار ہوئے اور پریشانی کی وجہ پوچھی۔ لکڑ ہارے نے سارا واقعہ سنایا۔ بزرگ نے پانی میں ڈبکی لگائی اور چاندی کی کلہاڑی نکال کر پوچھا: ”کیا یہ تمھاری ہے؟“ لکڑ ہارے نے کہا: ”نہیں، یہ میری نہیں۔“ پھر وہ سونے کی کلہاڑی لائے، لکڑ ہارے نے پھر انکار کر دیا۔ آخر میں وہ لوہے کی کلہاڑی لائے تو لکڑ ہارا خوش ہو کر بولا: ”ہاں، یہی میری کلہاڑی ہے۔“ بزرگ اس کی دیانت داری سے بہت خوش ہوئے اور انعام کے طور پر تینوں کلہاڑیاں اسے دے دیں۔ نتیجہ: دیانت داری کا پھل ہمیشہ میٹھا ہوتا ہے۔
